# Regular Expressions

## Regular Expressions as String Filters

Goals:

* Use regex to filter strings (and rows in a DataFrame).

* Read/write the core regex operators.

* See a regex as a set descriptor (a language over an alphabet).

* Build boolean masks: `df['col'].str.contains(pattern)`.

::: notes
Bridge from sets: a subset is just a predicate. Regex gives us predicates on strings.
:::

## From Sets to Strings

Sets:

* Math: $A=\{x\in U: P(x)\}$

* Strings: $L=\{w\in\Sigma^*: \texttt{matches}(w,\text{pattern})\}$

Key idea: A regular expression specifies membership in a set of strings using  patterns of characters.

We treat regex as both **filters** and as **languages**.

## Warm-Up: In or Out? {.activity}

`pattern = ^[A-Z]{2}\d{3}$`
$L=\{w\in\Sigma^*: \texttt{matches}(w,$ `  pattern`$)\}$

\ 

Which strings are in the set $L$?

\ 

`CS110`

`ab123`

`DS2200`

`MA101`

\

::: notes
This pattern says: start, 2 capital letters, 3 digits, end.
:::

## Standard Operators {.smaller}

Literals: `cat`

Dot: `.` any char (except newline)

Class: `[aeiou]` or ranges like `[A-Z0-9]`

Negated class: `[^,]` anything but comma

Alternation: `(cat|dog)`

Quantifiers: `a*` 0 or more, `a+` or more, `a?` 0 or 1, `{m,n}` range

Anchors: `^` start, `$` end

Escapes: `\.` literal dot

Groups: `(  )` captures, `(?:  )` non-capturing


## Regex vs. Language {.smaller}

Fix an alphabet of characters, $\Sigma$.

Then a language $L=\{w\in\Sigma^*: \texttt{matches}(w,$ `  pattern`$)\}$

* if a pattern matches nothing,  $L=\varnothing$

* `^$` matches only empty string ⇒ $L=\{\varepsilon\}$

* pattern `a` means $L=\{$`a`$\}$

* Concatenated patterns `AB` means $L(A)L(B)={xy:x\in L(A),y\in L(B)}$

* Union of patterns: `A|B` means $L(A)\cup L(B)$

* Kleene Star: `A*` means all finite concatenations from $L(A)$ (incl. $\varepsilon$)

::: notes
Same spirit as set algebra: union / product / closure.
:::

## Say the Set 

\ 

`^(ab|ba)*$`: strings over `{a,b}` that are concatenations of `ab` or `ba`.

\ 

`^(0|1)*11(0|1)*$`: all binary strings containing 11 as a substring.

\ 

`^1(01|10)*0$`: binary strings that start with 1, end with 0, and are filled with `{0,1}` pairs that flip from `1` to `0` or vice versa.


## Back to the Cafe

Suppose a column `drink` has values like:
<span class="rule">"Iced Latte", "Drip Coffee", "Americano", "Matcha Tea", "Espresso"</span>

\ 

Goals:

1. Keep espresso-style drinks: "espresso", "americano", "latte", or "cappuccino"

2. "Iced" appears as a whole word

3. Drinks that end with “Tea”

## Cafe continued

```{pyodide}
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UBC-CS/dsci220/refs/heads/main/data/cafe_orders.csv')

# regex
esprestr = r'(?i)\b(espresso|americano|latte|cappuccino)\b'
icedrestr = r'(?i)\biced\b'
tearestr = r'(?i)tea$'

# masks
espressoish = df['drink'].str.contains(esprestr, regex=True, na=False)
iced       = df['drink'].str.contains(icedstr,  regex=True, na=False)
teas       = df['drink'].str.contains(teastr,   regex=True, na=False)

# Set algebra on masks:
E_or_I   = espressoish | iced          # union
I_and_T  = iced & teas                 # intersection
not_I    = ~iced                       # complement

# Project the data:
subset = df[E_or_I]
subset
```

## Typical Patterns


Whole word: <span class="rule">r'\\biced\\b'</span>

Starts with: <span class="rule">r'^Iced'</span>

Ends with: <span class="rule">r'Tea$'</span>

Optional word: <span class="rule">r'^(Iced )?Latte$'</span>

One of set (case-insensitive):  

<center>
<span class="rule"> r'(?i)\\b(espresso|americano|latte|cappuccino)\\b'</span>
</center>

## Reminder: From Filter to Language {.smaller}

Let $\Sigma$ = letters, numbers, and spaces.

Pattern <span class="rule">^(?i)\b(espresso|americano|latte|cappuccino)\b$</span> denotes a language $L\subseteq \Sigma^*$.

This parallels:

Set: $L=\{,w\in\Sigma^*: \text{pattern matches},\}$

Predicate: $P(w)=\texttt{matches}(w,\text{pattern})$

Mask: <span class="rule">df['drink'].str.match(pattern)</span>

You’ve been doing language membership tests all class, with filters.
